Definition: The SDK built-in shell-execution tool, governed as a SECURITY_CONTROL and denied by default in Chirality.
Stance that Bash is denied by default even though the SDK ships the tool, enabled only after governance prerequisites are met.
Requirement that a denied Bash request must not create a child process; denial checks precede process creation.
Pre-execution governance step requiring mode/capability, timeout, stdout/stderr capture plan, result storage policy, and audit metadata before spawning.
Requirement that a timeout field or resolved timeout policy exist before a Bash command can start; numeric default/maximum are TBD.
Allowed Bash must capture standard output and standard error separately so output is distinguishable.
Policy that stores medium/large Bash output under session artifacts, represented by preview and safe metadata.
Permission record capturing decision, reason, source, timestamp, and optional safe metadata (TYPES.md 8.2).
Tool-list mechanism that is explicitly NOT a security boundary and cannot enable or restrict Bash by itself.
Mediation mechanism, alongside permission mode, policy, hooks, and canUseTool, that controls Bash enablement.
Approval-mediation hook used to govern Bash tool exposure.
Permission mode in which Bash should be unavailable or hard-denied.
Permission mode in which Bash denies without prompting; no approved safe-shell subset is defined in sources.
Permission mode in which Bash still needs explicit governance; write permission does not imply shell permission.
Developer-local-only permission mode, never ordinary shipped behavior, still subject to deny hooks and disallowed tools.
Posture where any explicit deny from policy, hook, path check, governance, SDK deny rule, or human gate blocks execution.
Behavior where hook failures block shell execution rather than allowing it.
Product-owned canonical audit records (.chirality/sessions/<sessionId>/events.jsonl) for runtime governance, primary over SDK transcripts.
Source-state warning on docs/PRD.md in _REFERENCES.md; PRD-derived details treated as warning-qualified until reconciled.
Scope item covered by DEL-06-05: Bash denied by default and governed when enabled.
Binding Bash invariant: default denial and enablement prerequisites in docs/CONTRACT.md Section 1.6.
Capability for allowed Bash to be interrupted/cancelled where supported; otherwise the actual terminal/residual-risk outcome is persisted.
Safe metadata (tool name, turn ID, byte count, truncation flag, relative artifact path) describing stored Bash output; channel labels and terminal-outcome linkage TBD.
